# `ref-inlined`

$ref replaced by an inline schema

| | |
|---|---|
| **Kind** | `sdk` |
| **Default severity** | `info` · `--profile sdk`: `error` |
| **Rule IDs** | `ref-inlined` |
| **Status** | Implemented (M5) |
| **Group** | References and components ([RULES.md section 8](../../RULES.md)) |

## What it detects

A `$ref` was replaced by an inline schema.

## Why this default

The named type disappears from generated SDKs (replaced by an anonymous one).

## Example

From test case [`ref-inlined`](../../test/cases/ref-inlined/): A $ref replaced by an identical inline schema: the named type disappears from generated SDKs.

`openapi.yaml`, base → revision:

```diff
  …
              application/json:
                schema:
-                 $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
+                 type: object
+                 properties:
+                   name:
+                     type: string
  components:
    schemas:
```

Findings:

- `ref-inlined` · info · GET /pets

## Test cases

The example above is the only test case for this rule.


## Policy options

Every rule takes `severity` (`error`, `warn`, `info` or `off`), `fix` and `explanation` in the policy file. The policy file arrives in M6; see [POLICY.md](../../POLICY.md).

```yaml
rules:
  ref-inlined: info
```

## How to fix

Keep the `$ref`.
